crime: Every night after lockup in their cell, {WITCH_NAME}'s roommate told a made-up story into the dark from the upper bunk, one hand hanging over the edge. From below, {WITCH_NAME} held that hand. Each night she pinched the story out of the air into a glass marble. The marbles lined her roommate's pillow and murmured her to sleep.
One night the girl stopped mid-story, drew her hand back up and said, "Go to sleep. I'll still be here in the morning."

{WITCH_NAME}'s father used to say that. He came home on random nights, tucked her in and said, "I'll still be here in the morning." She lay awake holding his sleeve, and every time she woke, his chair was empty.
She lay awake all that night. Before the doors opened, she climbed to the upper bunk and strangled her roommate with both hands until she was still.

When the doors opened at six, the prisoners called through the bars as they did every morning, and from under the blanket came, "Five more minutes." {WITCH_NAME} was already out in the cell corridor beside them, and she stayed among them all morning. When the girl missed breakfast, a prisoner went in to fetch her and lifted the blanket. She lay strangled and still warm among her murmuring marbles.
In the trial court, the prisoners concluded that someone had strangled her after she answered them, while {WITCH_NAME} was among them.

Then a prisoner picked up the marbles from the dead girl's pillow and held each one to her own ear. Every one held a night's story but one: a sleepy breath and "Five more minutes," over and over. The prisoners understood. The answer at the bars had been that marble, and the girl had died before the doors opened, locked in with {WITCH_NAME}.
fields.epitaph: She never let anyone stay long enough to keep the promise of morning.
fields.epithet: The night-keeper who never trusts the morning
execution: The execution stand raises a giant glass marble at the foot of a steep glass marble run. She is sealed inside, curled against the glass, facing the run. At the top, a giant shooter marble is let go. It rolls down the run, gathering speed, cracks into her marble and bursts through the glass into her. She lies still among the shards as the shooter rolls slowly to a stop beyond her.

magic.name: Moments in Glass
magic.text: She pinches the moment in front of her into a glass marble, where a tiny copy plays on, sounds and all.
